paper.title: UFO2: The Desktop AgentOS
paper.central_claim: A deeply OS-integrated multi-agent AgentOS for Windows (HostAgent + application-specialised AppAgents, UIA+vision hybrid control detection, unified GUI-API Puppeteer, retrieval-based knowledge integration, speculative multi-action execution, PiP isolation) outperforms prior CUAs including Operator: even with GPT-4o it reaches 27.9% on WAA and 28.6% on OSWorld-W (vs Operator 20.8/14.3) and cuts steps.

preliminary_evidence_judgment: Read before seat scores. UFO2 is a Windows multiagent system (HostAgent FSM, per-app AppAgents, UIA+OmniParser fusion, GUI/API Puppeteer, doc/experience RAG, speculative batches with UIA precondition checks, PiP desktop). Evaluation on WAA (154) and OSWorld-W (49, checker scripts corrected) with benchmark scripts and a 30-step cap for all agents. The full UFO2 row includes 'continuous knowledge augmentation', which uses 34 help documents 'tailored to benchmark tasks' with step-by-step instructions, 12 hand-written APIs for the OSWorld-W office tasks, and an experience DB filled from benchmark runs gated by an unvalidated LLM judge, none given to baselines. UFO2-base (no docs/APIs) beats Operator by 4 tasks on WAA. Ablation tables use differing base configurations (OSWorld-W 16.3 vs 22.4, the latter matching GUI+API); text claims o1 self-experience improves both benchmarks while Table 6 shows 25.3 -> 20.8 on WAA. Single runs.

signatures.object: Agent architecture and action interface on Windows: HostAgent (FSM, blackboard) delegating subtasks to per-application AppAgents whose Puppeteer chooses between registered native APIs and GUI actions.
signatures.information: Screenshots, UIA control metadata, SoM-annotated controls, OS process info; API registry; private and shared blackboard memory.
signatures.operation: Task decomposition into dependency-ordered subtasks; ReAct loop per AppAgent; API-first with GUI fallback; PENDING state for risky actions.
signatures.output: GUI event or API call per step.
signatures.conditions: App APIs exist (COM for Office) — 12 hand-written APIs for Word/Excel/PowerPoint; UIA available or visual fallback.
signatures.feedback: UIA state checks; execution result/error from API; user confirmation for risky steps.
signatures.selection_rule: Prefer semantically equivalent API; fallback on failure.
signatures.persistence: Session memory and blackboard within a session.
signatures.failure_boundary: Apps without APIs or UIA support (LibreOffice), plan errors on OSWorld-W.

signatures.object: Hybrid control detection: UIA controls plus OmniParser-v2 detections merged by IoU deduplication.
signatures.information: UIA tree + screenshot parsed by YOLOv8/Florence-2.
signatures.operation: Drop visual boxes with IoU>10% against UIA; wrap the rest as pseudo-UIA controls; SoM annotate.
signatures.output: Unified control list for the agent.
signatures.claimed_effect: Control Recovery Ratio 9.9% (WAA), up to 25% (OSWorld-W, o1).
signatures.failure_boundary: Vision-only worse than UIA on OSWorld-W (14.3 vs 22.4).

signatures.object: Knowledge substrate: help-document index and Example DB of summarised successful trajectories, retrieved into prompts.
signatures.information: 34 authored help docs tailored to benchmark tasks; past execution logs validated by an LLM Task Evaluator; retrieval top-1 doc, top-3 logs.
signatures.operation: Offline summarisation of success logs; embedding retrieval at run time.
signatures.claimed_effect: Plan Recovery Ratio up to 17.7%; WAA SR 23.4 -> 26.6.
signatures.failure_boundary: Benefit varies by model (o1 self-experience WAA 25.3 -> 20.8).

signatures.information: One LLM call predicts k actions; UIA validates each before execution.
signatures.operation: Batch predict, validate, execute, early-exit and replan.
signatures.selection_rule: First failed validation halts the batch

gap.author_gap: CUAs rely on screenshots and simulated input, ignoring accessibility/APIs and process state, and lock the user out of the desktop.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible and partially measured: 62% of WAA failures of the UIA-only base are control-detection failures and OSWorld-W errors are plan-heavy (author error analysis). The comparison with baselines is, however, a system-vs-system one with unequal access to APIs and authored knowledge.
lineage: UFO v1 (same group), NAVI/WAA, OmniAgent/OmniParser, Agent S, OpenAI Operator, Claude Computer Use - baselines in Table 1
gap.lineage_note: The pinned references.json contains no Windows desktop CUA; WAA/OSWorld numbers of baselines come from the paper and cited works; later work (UI-TARS-2, MAI-UI) is current_relevance only.
gap.closest_adjacent: UFO v1 (UIA + vision) and Agent S (hierarchy plus experience retrieval).
gap.residue: Latency (10 s/step LLM), UIA gaps in third-party apps, human-level gap.
gap.stakes: Practical desktop automation with non-disruptive execution.
gap.method_response: Make OS interfaces first-class: UIA+vision, APIs, FSM orchestration, retrieval knowledge, PiP.
gap.remaining_gap: Which components cause the gain once baselines get the same APIs and documents; test-task leakage in knowledge.
gap.aggregate_neighbor_check: Pinned AWM/SkillWeaver show prior induced workflow/skill memory; UFO2's residual is OS-level integration (UIA/API/FSM/PiP), not memory itself.

claims.text: UFO 2 outperforms Operator and other CUAs: WAA 27.9 vs 20.8; OSWorld-W 28.6 vs 14.3 (GPT-4o), 30.5/32.7 with o1.
claims.setting: WAA 154 tasks, OSWorld-W 49 tasks, 30 steps, benchmark scripts
claims.baseline_control: Five CUAs; baselines GPT-4o except Operator; UFO2 full includes 12 handwritten Office APIs (OSWorld-W), 34 task-tailored help docs and experience DB
claims.selection_vs_test: Knowledge and APIs authored for/derived from the evaluation tasks
claims.counterevidence: UFO2-base (no APIs, no docs) beats Operator by 2.6 (WAA) and 2.0 (OSWorld-W, one task); ablation baselines are inconsistent across tables.
claims.allowed_conclusion: UFO2 (authors configuration) scores higher than listed baselines on these two Windows benchmarks; the part attributable to OS integration as opposed to test-tailored resources is not separated.

claims.text: GUI+API raises success and reduces steps; hybrid detection recovers failures; knowledge integration reduces plan errors; speculation cuts steps by up to 51.5%.
claims.setting: OSWorld-W 49 tasks (APIs for 27 Office tasks) and WAA
claims.result_denominator: 49 and 154 tasks; ACS on subsets of 10-34 jointly solved tasks
claims.counterevidence: OSWorld-W UIA-only baselines are 22.4 (Tables 3, 6, 7) and 16.3 (Tables 1, 5); hybrid equals UIA SR for GPT-4o on OSWorld-W; o1 self-experience lowers WAA SR (25.3 -> 20.8).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Directionally plausible component benefits; magnitudes are not reliable.

claims.text: PiP isolation lets users work concurrently.
claims.counterevidence: No evaluation of PiP or safeguard.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: WAA and OSWorld-W live tasks scored by the benchmarks' verification scripts (OSWorld-W scripts corrected by the authors); single platform (Windows), knowledge tailored to benchmark tasks, so not transfer.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported single runs with a common 30-step cap: UFO2-base (UIA, GUI-only, no knowledge) slightly exceeds Operator and other GPT-4o CUAs on WAA (23.4 vs 20.8); full UFO2 reaches 27.9/28.6 with GPT-4o, but its margin includes benchmark-tailored help documents and hand-built APIs unavailable to baselines; per-module tables show small gains (often 1-4 tasks) and reduced steps on jointly solved subsets.
not_supported: Architecture-attributable superiority of full UFO2 over baselines under equal information
Self-experience improving o1 on both benchmarks (Table 6 contradicts)
Generalisation to unseen apps or other OSes
unresolved: Temporal separation of the experience DB from test tasks
assessment.retention_trace: before: base agent -> candidates: successful benchmark trajectories -> selection: unvalidated LLM Task Evaluator -> persisted: per-app example DB -> later use: retrieved (top-3) for benchmark tasks -> measured: Table 6 (mixed). No temporal/test separation stated, so retained improvement is not established.

G.reason: Both seats: concrete systems gap (no accessibility/API state, disruptive control) tied to a measured failure breakdown; broad continuous-improvement rhetoric outpaces residual proof.

M.reason: Both seats: each module has a mechanism and a checkable signal (UIA preconditions, API-first routing, IoU fusion, FSM states); bundle-level problem-fit only partly tested.

X.reason: Both seats: architecture, FSMs, fusion rule, API registry, retrieval and speculation loop reconstructable; full-configuration composition per benchmark and API/GUI selection policy underspecified.

E.measurement.reason: Success is decided by the benchmarks' own verification scripts under a common 30-step cap, the right instrument for the online claim. Deductions: OSWorld-W scripts were corrected without validation, ablation tables silently use different base configurations (OSWorld-W 16.3 vs 22.4, the latter equal to GUI+API), and the text misstates Table 6. These are reporting/scope issues around a sound checker, consistent with the 3 given to RCI's MiniWoB++ reward with copied baselines, not anchor 2.

E.causality.reason: Both seats: per-module on/off tables and Operator-as-AppAgent, but baselines receive neither APIs nor tailored docs, base configurations differ across tables, gains of 1-3 tasks.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats: help documents tailored to benchmark tasks, APIs built for the benchmark office tasks, experience DB filled from benchmark runs without stated separation; no unseen apps/OS.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats: single runs, 2-point OSWorld-W increments are single tasks, joint-success subsets of 7-34 tasks, error-type percentages without denominators.

E.cost.reason: Common 30-step cap, step counts on jointly solved subsets, per-stage latency (LLM ~10 s per call, +1 s hybrid detection) and hardware are reported. Not 3: the manual engineering budget (34 benchmark-tailored documents, 12 APIs) that the full system receives and baselines do not is unaccounted, token/dollar and failure-inclusive costs are missing, and the ~1 minute per task figure does not reconcile with the per-step latencies.
